intro_html:
The best things to do in Kanazawa are not just the famous things. A strong first trip usually needs one major garden-and-castle block, one historic quarter that you let breathe, one regional meal, and one quieter cultural stop that keeps the city from becoming all scenery and no texture.

This is the edited answer to the broad query itself: what to do in Kanazawa, what to see first, and how to use a short trip without spending the city in the wrong order.

facts.label: Best balance move
facts.value: Pair history with a serious food stop

todos.title: Anchor the trip around one full morning in the garden and castle zone
todos.body: Kanazawa feels clearer once you have seen Kenroku-en and the castle grounds properly. That first block gives the rest of the city scale and logic.

todos.title: Treat the old quarters as neighborhoods, not photo stops
todos.body: Higashiyama and Nagamachi are at their best when you let them work as walks, tea stops, and mood-setting districts rather than quick passes.

todos.title: Use one meal to understand the region, not just to fill a gap
todos.body: Omicho seafood, nodoguro, crab season, and Kaga cuisine are part of why Kanazawa matters. Let one lunch or dinner carry that weight.

attractions.name: Kenroku-en and Kanazawa Castle
attractions.hook: If you only give one part of Kanazawa real time, give it to the garden-and-castle block.
attractions.description: Kenroku-en is one of Japan's great gardens, but the real value for a first trip is how well it works with the castle grounds beside it. Together they give Kanazawa its scale and visual identity in one sweep.
attractions.tip: Arrive early and let the walk run naturally from garden to castle before the rest of the city fills in.

attractions.name: Higashi Chaya and the hillside temple walk
attractions.hook: This is the district that makes Kanazawa feel preserved rather than reconstructed.
attractions.description: Higashi Chaya works best when you combine the teahouse streets with the quieter temple trail behind them. That pairing turns the area from a photogenic street into a proper half-day with depth.
attractions.tip: Go early if you want the quarter before the busiest foot traffic arrives.

attractions.name: Nagamachi and the samurai layer of the city
metas: Easy to pair with the castle area
attractions.hook: The samurai quarter is the best reminder that Kanazawa's preservation is social as well as architectural.
attractions.description: Nagamachi works because it feels intentionally restrained. Earthen walls, stone lanes, and the Nomura residence show the city from a different angle than the geisha quarters.
attractions.tip: Use this after the castle side of the city rather than treating it as a separate day.

attractions.name: Omicho Market and a serious seafood meal
attractions.badge: Do not skip the food angle
attractions.hook: Kanazawa is not fully understood until you let the Sea of Japan onto the itinerary.
attractions.description: Omicho Market is the obvious entry point, but the bigger lesson is that Kanazawa's food culture is serious enough to shape the trip. Seafood breakfasts, Kaga cuisine lunches, and winter crab or nodoguro nights all belong in the city answer.
attractions.tip: Use the market early, then save one second meal for a slower, more deliberate dinner.

attractions.name: One slower cultural counterweight
attractions.hook: Kanazawa gets better when one stop is chosen for texture, not scale.
attractions.description: For some travelers that is the 21st Century Museum; for others it is Myoryuji, a tea stop in Higashiyama, or the D.T. Suzuki Museum. The point is to give the city one quieter or stranger note.
attractions.tip: Use this pick to shape day two once the essential historic layer is already in place.

getting_there.text: The historic core is compact enough that the best Kanazawa trips are mostly walk-led once you have reached the center.
The Loop Bus helps at the start and end of the day, but overusing it can make a small city feel more complicated than it is.
If you only have two days, cut the day trip before you cut the old quarters or the food side of the city.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Kanazawa for a first visit?
faqs.a: The strongest first trip usually includes Kenroku-en and the castle, one geisha or samurai district, a seafood or Kaga-cuisine meal, and one quieter cultural stop that adds depth beyond the postcard version of the city.

faqs.q: How many days do you need for the best things to do in Kanazawa?
faqs.a: Two full days covers the core very well. Three days is the sweet spot if you want the city plus one slower cultural stop or a short day trip.

faqs.q: What should I book in advance in Kanazawa?
faqs.a: Myoryuji, often called the Ninja Temple, is the main booking that can shape your schedule. Most other major sights in Kanazawa are straightforward walk-ins.
